question: Should we do what the Pharisees say to do?
summary: Matthew 23:1-3 has Jesus tell the crowds that because the scribes and Pharisees 'sit in Moses' seat,' the listeners should 'observe and do' whatever the Pharisees tell them — just don't imitate their behavior. Matthew 16:12, by contrast, has the disciples finally understand Jesus' warning that they should beware 'the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.' Same gospel, two opposite instructions about whether to follow Pharisaic teaching.

reconcile.connective: Tyndale's notes read the charge as conditional, not absolute — obey only what tracks Mosaic law, or read it as irony or tactical restraint.

discrepancy.connective: Anthony Saldarini reads 23:2-3 as an unassimilated fragment of the Matthean community's residual synagogue loyalty — a layer the Gospel's blanket anti-Pharisaic verdict never absorbs.

skeptic.name: Anthony J. Saldarini
skeptic.attribution: Anthony J. Saldarini, Matthew's Christian-Jewish Community (University of Chicago Press, 1994)

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's 'Ethical Discrepancies' chapter pairs Matthew 23:2-3 verbatim under a two-column heading, 'Rendered to the scribes. / They must be shunned,' set against the parallel warning to beware the scribes (Mark 12:38-40), resolved with the identical doctrine/practice split this row's own reconcile note uses: 'The idea is, Follow their precepts, but shun their practice. Do as they say, but not as they do.'

excerpts.excerpt_text: This was not a blanket endorsement of all that the Pharisees teach (see 15:1-20; 16:5-12; 23:13-39). It might refer only to what was in accord with the law of Moses, or it might be bitter irony or sarcasm. Jesus might also have been counseling conformity to the Pharisees’ teachings to avoid giving offense (17:24-27).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly cross-references 16:5-12 (which includes 16:12) and offers three distinct harmonizing readings for the exact obey-vs-beware tension the row states, rather than merely glossing the verse in isolation.
